ops.body:
Independently re-verified and closed 2026-07-25. Shipped in 491244e, released as codex 1.8.4.

Re-measured the golden myself on the reconciled tree rather than accepting the implementing lane's numbers: 15/15 consecutive isolated runs at default GOGC, plus 6/6 at GOGC=1 — the setting that reproduced the bug 10/10 before the fix. 21/21 total. The flake is cured at the cause, not masked.

Worth preserving as a diagnostic lesson: my own narrowing was confidently wrong in its conclusion while being right in its method. Elimination over the exit-1 paths correctly established that the replacement could not legitimately reach the busy check while the first process held LOCK_EX — but I read that as "it must be dying inside acquireLaneLock" when the real answer was that the premise had failed: the first process was no longer holding the lock at all, because the GC had closed the fd underneath it. An impossible-looking observation meant an invariant had broken, not that the reachable code paths were mis-enumerated.

The EINTR hypothesis was refuted properly rather than merely abandoned — a C probe on this host showed Darwin restarts flock transparently under SA_RESTART, and Go installs every handler including SIGURG that way, so the mechanism cannot occur in this binary. Declining to add a retry loop on the unproven hypothesis was the right call; it would have shipped dead code and left the real bug live. Note the residual: on Linux flock is not restarted even with SA_RESTART, so a retry loop would be correct hardening there — worth doing if codex-ask ever ships beyond darwin, but as hardening, not as a fix for this.

Also fixed in passing: the golden asserted at test_scaffold.py:1398 before calling communicate(), discarding the subprocess output that turned out to be the one piece of evidence that cracked this. It now reports the replacement's rc, stdout, and stderr on failure.
